title: An invertible relation block eliminates fixed generators on a principal open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $a,b\geq0$, and $\pi:A^{\oplus(a+b)}\twoheadrightarrow M$ a surjective $A$-linear map. Write $m_j=\pi(e_j)$ for the standard generators. Let $(C\ D)$ be an $a\times(a+b)$ matrix [def-weil-matrix], with $C$ square of size $a$, such that every row lies in $\ker\pi$. Put $\delta=\det C$, using the determinant of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Let $A_\delta=A[1/\delta]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $M_\delta$ be the localization at the powers of $\delta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then in $M_\delta$, with $x=(m_1/1,\ldots,m_a/1)$ and $y=(m_{a+1}/1,\ldots,m_{a+b}/1)$, one has $\delta x+\operatorname{adj}(C)Dy=0$ and $x=-\delta^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(C)Dy$, where the adjugate has entries $\operatorname{adj}(C)_{ij}=(-1)^{i+j}\det(C^{(j,i)})$, where $C^{(j,i)}$ is obtained by deleting row $j$ and column $i$ of $C$. In particular, the last $b$ elements $m_{a+1}/1,\ldots,m_{a+b}/1$ generate $M_\delta$. Moreover, on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\widetilde M$ and its canonical sections $\tau(m_j)$ be those of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The restrictions of $\tau(m_{a+1}),\ldots,\tau(m_{a+b})$ generate $\widetilde M|_{D(\delta)}$ as a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. This includes $a=0$ with $\delta=1$, and $b=0$ with $M_\delta=0$. No finite generation assumption on $\ker\pi$ is made.

proof.text: Each row relation says $\sum_{i=1}^a C_{ki}m_i+\sum_{j=1}^bD_{kj}m_{a+j}=0$ in $M$. Apply the linear map $m\mapsto m/1$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], obtaining $Cx+Dy=0$. Multiply its $k$th equation by $\operatorname{adj}(C)_{ik}$ and sum over $k$. Distribute and interchange the finite sums; [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives $\sum_k\operatorname{adj}(C)_{ik}C_{k\ell}=\delta\,\mathbf1_{i=\ell}$. Thus $\delta x+\operatorname{adj}(C)Dy=0$, with precisely the cofactor convention in that cited statement.

proof.text: By [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $\delta/1$ is a unit of $A_\delta$ with inverse $1/\delta$. Multiply the preceding identity by its inverse to get $x=-\delta^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(C)Dy$. Every element of $M_\delta$ is $m/\delta^n$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; surjectivity of $\pi$ writes $m=\sum_{i=1}^{a+b}r_i m_i$. Substitute the displayed expression for each of the first $a$ generators, so $m/\delta^n$ is an $A_\delta$-linear combination of the last $b$. If $a=0$, the determinant is $1$ by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], and the original surjection gives the conclusion. If $b=0$, the combination is empty, so every localized element is zero. This also covers the zero ring and $\delta=0$.

proof.text: Construct the canonical compatible family of last-generator sections on D(delta). To show its free map is epic, let p and q be two maps out of the restricted tilde M agreeing after that free map. They agree on every last-generator section. Apply step 1 already in M and then the canonical map to sections on any open V contained in D(delta). Its adjugate identity, linearity of p and q, and invertibility of delta in the structure ring on V imply that p and q also agree on every first-generator section. The original module surjection pi is the finite sum of coordinate projections followed by the maps A -> M sending 1 to each original generator. Apply the additive tilde functor and the additive restriction functor. The tilde adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]; compose it with Mathlib's restriction adjunction SheafOfModules.overPushforwardOverAdj. The elementary Hom-adjunction argument Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_of_adjunction shows that the composite sends pi to an epimorphism. For each coordinate summand, naturality of the canonical sections from [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] identifies its value on 1 with that generator section; ring-linearity shows that p and q agree on the entire summand. Hence they agree after the image of pi, and cancellation of that epimorphism gives p=q. This is the epimorphism of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. The proof includes empty D(delta) and empty index sets without case distinctions.
